scope: Unit author identity hypotheses at submission; not independent acceptance

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces two independently owned consumers react to a committed closure snapshot, while the host cannot know or call them directly.
items.decisiveFact: Two independently owned consumers react to a committed closure snapshot, while the host cannot know or call them directly.
items.nearestAlternative: Direct calls work for a fixed pair, but they couple the session host to both modules and violate the stated ownership boundary.
items.changedCondition: If export were the only synchronous step and the host owned it, a direct call could be simpler.
items.identityReason: The original whiteboard close/export domain and stable-session fact remain; this revision makes independently owned subscribers and post-commit observation the decision.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces two separately owned consumers need the same accepted ownership/deadline change without a direct dependency between them.
items.decisiveFact: Two separately owned consumers need the same accepted ownership/deadline change without a direct dependency between them.
items.nearestAlternative: A coordinator can call both systems, but it would become a shared owner of two team-specific update APIs.
items.changedCondition: If only one worklist were part of the service, a direct update could be sufficient.
items.identityReason: The source escalation and paired ownership/deadline facts are retained; the item now targets fan-out to independently maintained consumers.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces consumers may react only after both listing validations succeed and the listing is ready to publish.
items.decisiveFact: Consumers may react only after both listing validations succeed and the listing is ready to publish.
items.nearestAlternative: Notifying as each field changes gives faster updates, but exposes incomplete listing state to both consumers.
items.changedCondition: If consumers were meant to display draft progress, interim field notifications could be appropriate.
items.identityReason: The source marketplace listing and price/stock facts are retained; the new focus is the valid publication boundary seen by independent subscribers.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces three independent consumers need the same accepted split facts, including the stable request identity and delivery promise.
items.decisiveFact: Three independent consumers need the same accepted split facts, including the stable request identity and delivery promise.
items.nearestAlternative: Letting inventory notify vendors and vendors notify customer status creates a chain where one consumer becomes another's dispatcher.
items.changedCondition: If one service owned all three follow-up actions, direct sequencing could be simpler.
items.identityReason: The source backorder-split case and its identity/promise invariant are retained; this version asks how independent systems receive one accepted split.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces two read models need the same approved transfer details, but the reservation remains the owner of the decision.
items.decisiveFact: Two read models need the same approved transfer details, but the reservation remains the owner of the decision.
items.nearestAlternative: Letting the allocation board make the transfer and then inform the audit view would move decision ownership into a consumer.
items.changedCondition: If the board owned both approval and audit behavior, it could coordinate them directly.
items.identityReason: The source plot-transfer facts remain, while the candidate makes the separation between decision owner and two reacting views concrete.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces two modules need the same validated bundle version after its component rules are valid.
items.decisiveFact: Two modules need the same validated bundle version after its component rules are valid.
items.nearestAlternative: Having billing poll the catalog couples billing to catalog storage and may expose a version before validation finishes.
items.changedCondition: If billing were the only consumer and owned bundle changes, a direct call could be simpler.
items.identityReason: The source bundle pricing-policy fact is retained; the revised question tests how separately owned modules react to one validated version.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces two independently maintained views need the same reservation identity after capacity and expiry checks succeed.
items.decisiveFact: Two independently maintained views need the same reservation identity after capacity and expiry checks succeed.
items.nearestAlternative: The mobile view can call the grid dashboard after confirmation, but it does not own grid operations and would become its relay.
items.changedCondition: If one view were owned by the coordinator and there were no separate dashboard, a direct update might suffice.
items.identityReason: The source charger reservation/capacity/expiry case is preserved; the revised decision is the post-validation fan-out of a stable confirmation fact.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces independent downstream modules need the committed descriptive revision, while asset identity remains stable and service code must not name them.
items.decisiveFact: Independent downstream modules need the committed descriptive revision, while asset identity remains stable and service code must not name them.
items.nearestAlternative: A search-index update can call thumbnail generation afterward, but the index does not own thumbnails and can fail before its peer runs.
items.changedCondition: If both modules were part of one synchronous asset-service operation, a direct call could be adequate.
items.identityReason: The source photo-archive metadata and stable identity are retained; the new focus is independent consumers reacting to the same committed revision.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces two independent consumers need the same approved scope and attribution after the licensing decision.
items.decisiveFact: Two independent consumers need the same approved scope and attribution after the licensing decision.
items.nearestAlternative: The report can call the dashboard with its computed view, but that couples two consumers and makes the report own approval distribution.
items.changedCondition: If the dashboard were the only consumer and part of the approval service, a direct call could be sufficient.
items.identityReason: The source territory/expiry approval facts remain; this revision tests publication of the accepted scope and attribution to independent teams.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces both consumers need the accepted battery assignment only after the single-aircraft check succeeds.
items.decisiveFact: Both consumers need the accepted battery assignment only after the single-aircraft check succeeds.
items.nearestAlternative: The availability board can announce the assignment first and let maintenance catch up, but it does not own the replacement decision.
items.changedCondition: If a battery's assignment had no dependent views, a direct update without notification might be adequate.
items.identityReason: The source battery replacement and unique aircraft-assignment fact are retained; the item now specifies how independent views learn the accepted assignment.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces two separate consumers need the named recipient and exact consent revision only after the navigator approves disclosure.
items.decisiveFact: Two separate consumers need the named recipient and exact consent revision only after the navigator approves disclosure.
items.nearestAlternative: The appointment planner can ask the audit view for consent details, but the audit view is not the consent authority.
items.changedCondition: If appointment planning were part of the navigator's own workflow, a direct call might fit.
items.identityReason: The source referral/privacy boundary is retained; the revision emphasizes fan-out of the consented recipient and revision to independent consumers.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces two consumers need one completed attempt tied to its exercise and scoring versions, while the tracker cannot call their implementations.
items.decisiveFact: Two consumers need one completed attempt tied to its exercise and scoring versions, while the tracker cannot call their implementations.
items.nearestAlternative: Letting analytics poll current learner progress loses the exact attempt and may observe a later policy version.
items.changedCondition: If the tracker owned both views and completion were synchronous, direct updates could be simpler.
items.identityReason: The source timed-exercise and version/policy facts remain; the candidate asks how independent consumers react to the same completed attempt.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces two independent consumers need the same accepted, attributable exception after approval, while purchasing retains decision authority.
items.decisiveFact: Two independent consumers need the same accepted, attributable exception after approval, while purchasing retains decision authority.
items.nearestAlternative: Letting compliance call the dashboard would make an audit consumer responsible for another team's view.
items.changedCondition: If the dashboard were the only consumer and part of the purchasing service, a direct update could suffice.
items.identityReason: The source bounded/attributable procurement exception remains; the case now separates approval authority from post-approval notification to two independently owned views.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces two consumers need the exact annotation-map revision after reviewers accept the recording replacement.
items.decisiveFact: Two consumers need the exact annotation-map revision after reviewers accept the recording replacement.
items.nearestAlternative: Search can call transcript rendering after indexing, but that couples consumers and does not identify the accepted map revision.
items.changedCondition: If transcript rendering were part of the search module and had one owner, direct sequencing could suffice.
items.identityReason: The source recording replacement and stable-segment map are retained; this version focuses on consistent reaction to one approved mapping revision.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces three independent consumers react to one approved role expiry, each for its own view or record.
items.decisiveFact: Three independent consumers react to one approved role expiry, each for its own view or record.
items.nearestAlternative: The access-control view can call audit and administrator modules, but it would become the dispatcher for other teams' responsibilities.
items.changedCondition: If the access-control module owned all three updates, direct calls could be simpler.
items.identityReason: The source temporary-role/approval case is retained; the revised learner decision is fan-out of one expiry fact to independent consumers.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces independent consumers need the same exact association between a completed seal and its immutable revision.
items.decisiveFact: Independent consumers need the same exact association between a completed seal and its immutable revision.
items.nearestAlternative: The archive catalog can call the portal after saving, but one consumer should not own another consumer's UI update.
items.changedCondition: If the portal were just a view inside the archive catalog, a direct local refresh could be sufficient.
items.identityReason: The source notarization case's exact immutable revision remains; the proposal focuses on notifying two independent views of the completed association.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces two independent consumers need one accepted payout/order association after the payout owner releases it.
items.decisiveFact: Two independent consumers need one accepted payout/order association after the payout owner releases it.
items.nearestAlternative: Seller history can ask finance reporting to update after it records the payout, but neither consumer should dispatch the other's work.
items.changedCondition: If finance reporting were part of seller history's own module, direct sequencing could work.
items.identityReason: The source payout's settled-order and release facts remain; the proposal tests how independent consumers receive the completed association.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces a late subscriber needs one current snapshot followed by future changes, not the full historical stream as fresh changes.
items.decisiveFact: A late subscriber needs one current snapshot followed by future changes, not the full historical stream as fresh changes.
items.nearestAlternative: Replaying every old announcement is useful for an archive, but it can make a live display show obsolete platforms before the current one.
items.changedCondition: If the consumer were an audit log that must reconstruct history, full historical replay could be appropriate.
items.identityReason: The source transit disruption domain remains; this item distinguishes a live subscriber's initial current view from historical replay.
